Ornement du chapiteau de la colonne ionique et de la colonne composite, fait en forme de spirale.

examples.text: L’acanthe de Corinthe, la volute d’Ionie fleurissaient et se contournaient au chapiteau des colonnes.
De chaque côté s’élevaient des maisons de brique rouge surmontées de pignons à volutes, dont les fenêtres et les portes se détachaient, encadrées de blanc, avec une propreté toute hollandaise.
À première vue, on attribuerait au gothique flamboyant cette maîtresse œuvre où l’on découvre bientôt les volutes, les ornements, toutes les riches imaginations de la Renaissance.

glosses: Ornement en forme de spirale, à l’extrémité du manche d’un violon, viole, violoncelle ou contrebasse.
Nom donné à des coquilles univalves tournées en cône pyramidal.
Spirale, tourbillon, d’un fluide, fumée, brume, etc.

examples.text: Lorsque Jasper Hobson arriva sur les bords du lagon, il ne put en distinguer la surface, qui était encore cachée par de grosses volutes de brumes.
[…]; les volutes de brume qui coiffaient les volcans furent alors éclairées en rouge, donnant à l’ensemble de l’île l’aspect d’une formidable éruption générale.
Marandier alluma une cigarette et suivit d’un regard rêveur les volutes bleues qui serpentinaient vers le plafond.

translations.source_sense_description: Ornement du chapiteau d'une colonne, en forme de spirale

glosses: ein schneckenförmiges eingerolltes Zierelement von Bauteilen wie Konsolen, Giebeln oder Kapitellen

examples.text: „In der Baukunst des Barock wurden Voluten in vielfältiger Weise als schmückende Elemente verwendet.“
„Alles ist hier verschroben, üppig, zu Voluten eingerollt, barock und bewegt.“

translations.source_sense_description: Ornement du chapiteau d'une colonne, en forme de spirale

glosses: The characteristic spiral curve on an Ionic capital, widely copied in other styles and in neoclassical architecture.

examples.text: This example is much richer, yet no less elegant, than the other; the volute, instead of a single spiral, is formed by three; the sculptured echinus beneath is surmounted by a guilloched moulding, and separated from the shaft by a neck […]

glosses: The spirals or whorls on a gastropod's shell.
Any marine gastropod of the family Volutidae.

examples.text: Common shells include frog-shells, distorsios, volutes, tulips, murex, cones, olives, marginellas, cowries, augers and the Florida horse conch, the state's official shell, which can grow up to 24in (6 1 cm) long.

glosses: The casing in a centrifugal pump, whose shape is somewhat similar to architectural volutes.
A spiral or scroll form.
A scroll-shaped carving at the tuning head of a stringed musical instrument, similar to architectural volutes.
Of a spring: having a spiral curve on its tail.
Rolled up in any way.

translations.source_sense_description: Ornement du chapiteau d'une colonne, en forme de spirale

glosses: A roll of paper or parchment; a writing formed into a roll.
An ornament formed of undulations giving off spirals or sprays, usually suggestive of plant form. Roman architectural ornament is largely of some scroll pattern.
Spirals or sprays in the shape of an actual plant.

examples.text:
I lose myself
in a flawed henna plant
jutting toward the scroll.
Its rose-pink eyes burst
off the stems.

glosses: A mark or flourish added to a person's signature, intended to represent a seal, and in some States allowed as a substitute for a seal. [U.S.] Alexander Mansfield Burrill.
The carved end of a violin, viola, cello or other stringed instrument, most commonly scroll-shaped but occasionally in the form of a human or animal head.
A skew surface.
A kind of sweet roll baked in a somewhat spiral shape.

examples.text: I ordered a glass of lemonade and a coffee scroll.

glosses: The incremental movement of graphics on a screen, removing one portion to show the next.

examples.text: […] the computer sends orders, via electrical impulses, to recompose the liquid crystal structure inside the cells quickly which results in the familiar smooth scroll of the pointer on your screen.

glosses: A spiral waterway placed round a turbine to regulate the flow.
A turbinate bone.
A rough draft of anything.
The act of scrolling

examples.text: I gave the terms and conditions a quick scroll before signing up to the website.

glosses: To change one's view of data on a computer's display by moving in gradual increments, typically using an input device or touch screen.

examples.text: She scrolled the offending image out of view.
She kept scrolling until she found the desired paragraph.

glosses: To move in or out of view horizontally or vertically.

examples.text: The rising credits slowly scrolled off the screen.
The piano plays on. I watch those little rectangles as they scroll down from the top.
Pavement scrolled beneath the headlight beams, reminding Emma of a conveyor belt.

glosses: To flood a chat system with numerous lines of text, causing legitimate messages to scroll out of view before they can be read.

examples.text: Hey, stop scrolling!

glosses: geschwungene Verzierung

examples.text: Der Bilderrahmen war voller Schnörkel.
„Mit dem Finger malte er Schnörkel auf die Theke.“
„Ein Rest von Bemalung, ein kläglicher ausgewachsener Schnörkel belehrten mich, daß dieses Haus in fernen Friedens- und Sommerzeiten afrikanische Kunden bedient hatte.“

„Wir erachten es als selbstverständlich, dass wir unsere Gedanken in einen Haufen willkürlicher Schnörkel zwängen, die die Zeilen eines Blattes Papier oder eines Bildschirms bevölkern, und dass dieselben Schnörkel wiederum in den Köpfen oder Kehlen anderer Menschen am anderen Ende der Welt oder in einer fernen unbekannten Zukunft zum Leben erwachen können.“

glosses: schneckenförmige Verzierung der Geigen

examples.text: Bei dieser Geige war statt eines Schnörkels ein Engelskopf.

translations.source_sense_description: (Figuré) Spirale, tourbillon, d’un fluide, fumée, brume, etc.

glosses: A curve that is the locus of a point that rotates about a fixed point while continuously increasing its distance from that point.
A helix.
A self-sustaining process with a lot of momentum involved, so it is difficult to accelerate or stop it at once.

examples.text: My beloved friends and family who sustained and grounded me as I fell into the rabbit hole of this project or down the spiral of new parenthood.

glosses: A section of track that forms a circle and crosses over itself, used for gaining height in mountainous territory.
Helical, like a spiral.

examples.text: The formation of tornados and water-spouts is very probably identical with that of dust-storms and "devils," viz., a sudden disturbance of the vertical equilibrium of the atmosphere, where by an upward rush of air is generated, which rapidly becomes spiral.

glosses: To move along the path of a spiral or helix.

examples.text: The falling leaves spiralled down from the tree.

glosses: To cause something to spiral.

examples.text: You need to learn how to spiral a ball.

glosses: To increase continually.

examples.text: Her debts were spiralling out of control.
